Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz / 40 fps lock pairs perfectly with the LCD panel and gives a smooth, judder-free feel; FSR at 1024x640 keeps image quality high while leaving GPU headroom for busy combat scenes.

profiles.Summary: Divinity: Original Sin 2 – Definitive Edition runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, with the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeding the game's minimum GPU requirements; the isometric RPG style keeps GPU load manageable even at higher settings. The game is CPU-light enough during exploration but can spike during large combat encounters with many physics and spell effects.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements compared against Deck GPU capability (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class, comfortably above the GTX 550 minimum and approaching the GTX 770 recommended). On your first run, check frame rate during a large outdoor combat encounter — if it dips below your cap, reduce Shadow Quality and Ambient Occlusion first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling with FSR keeps the GPU well within a 7 W TDP; the isometric camera means FSR softening is barely noticeable. Ideal for long sessions away from a charger.

KnownIssues: Text and UI elements can appear small at native 1280x800; increasing the UI scale in options is recommended.
Large combat encounters with many simultaneous spell effects may cause brief frame dips.
Split-screen co-op is significantly more demanding on the GPU and may require lower settings than single-player.
Some players report occasional stutters on first load of a new area, likely due to shader compilation under Proton.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with ultra settings the Deck GPU generally holds 55-60 fps in exploration and open areas; expect dips to the low 50s or high 40s in large multi-character combat with heavy spell effects. Drop Shadow Quality to Medium if dips are unacceptable.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay that suits the turn-based pacing; upscaling from 1024x640 recovers enough headroom to keep textures and shadows at medium-high without thermal throttling. This is the recommended daily-driver profile.

profiles.Summary: Divinity: Original Sin 2 – Definitive Edition runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, benefiting from full controller support and a relatively modest GPU requirement that the Deck's RDNA 2 hardware handles comfortably. The isometric RPG style keeps GPU load manageable, and 40–60 fps is achievable across a range of quality settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 770 / R9 280 recommended, which the Deck's GPU roughly matches) and the game's isometric, turn-based nature. On first run, check frame pacing during a large outdoor area or a multi-enemy combat encounter, and drop to the Optimal profile if you see sustained dips below 35 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU and TDP low for maximum session length; the isometric camera means FSR artefacts are barely noticeable. Half-rate shading is left off as it causes visible shimmer on the game's detailed character models.

KnownIssues: Some players report occasional stuttering during large-scale combat encounters with many particle effects on screen.
The game's launcher may occasionally appear on first launch — selecting 'Play' and setting options before closing resolves this.
Split-screen co-op can significantly increase GPU load and may require lower settings to stay stable.
No native Wayland/Vulkan path; runs via DirectX 11 through Proton, which is stable but adds a small translation overhead.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full 1280x800 with high/ultra settings the Deck sustains 50-60 fps in most areas, though dense combat scenes with many spell effects can dip to the mid-40s; the 60 fps cap prevents runaway GPU usage. Battery life is short at full TDP, so keep a charger handy for long sessions.
